import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Check if any feature shows significant association with outcome
    significant_features = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, i], feats.y)[0, 1]) > 0.05:
            significant_features.append(fid)
    
    # If no significant features, return empty design
    if not significant_features:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Check for correlation among features to avoid near-duplicates
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    correlated_pairs = set()
    for i in range(len(feats.ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(feats.ids)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i, j]) >= 0.6:
                fid_i, fid_j = feats.ids[i], feats.ids[j]
                correlated_pairs.add((min(fid_i, fid_j), max(fid_i, fid_j)))
    
    # Remove near-duplicates
    unique_features = []
    for fid in significant_features:
        is_duplicate = False
        for existing_fid in unique_features:
            if (min(fid, existing_fid), max(fid, existing_fid)) in correlated_pairs:
                is_duplicate = True
                break
        if not is_duplicate:
            unique_features.append(fid)
    
    # If no unique features remain, return empty design
    if not unique_features:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Fit logistic regression with all unique features
    X = feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in unique_features]]
    model = LogisticRegression(fit_intercept=True, max_iter=1000)
    
    # Cross-validate to get stable coefficients
    skf = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)
    coefs = []
    for train_idx, _ in skf.split(X, feats.y):
        X_train = X[train_idx]
        y_train = feats.y[train_idx]
        model.fit(X_train, y_train)
        coefs.append(model.coef_[0])
    
    # Average coefficients
    avg_coefs = np.mean(coefs, axis=0)
    
    # Sort by absolute coefficient value to identify potential drivers
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(np.abs(avg_coefs))[::-1]
    
    # Select top features as drivers (at most MAX_DRIVERS)
    drivers = tuple([unique_features[i] for i in sorted_indices[:MAX_DRIVERS]])
    
    # For columns, use all features that were used in fitting
    columns = tuple(unique_features)
    
    # No products needed
    products = ()
    
    # Loadings based on standardized coefficients
    loadings = dict(zip(unique_features, avg_coefs))
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
